utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I am. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today when we'll begin with your finding regarding Markale I and II; that's 1D05496. We see the report on our screens. Because of the long introduction and your CV, we will move to page 133 immediately. That's where the report begins. In B/C/S. And, in English, it's page 130.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 3-0 in English and 3-3 in B/C/S, please. From some reason, Your Honours, this report does not have figures in English version. We couldn't change it since CLSS did it that way. So I will always have to have B/C/S version at the same time to be able to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll do our utmost best to -- sometimes it's even an advantage, it seems, to the left the figure or the sketch, and to the right the text. But we'll -- we'll try to do everything as good as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, would you tell us, in your view, what is characteristic of the incident involving the explosion on the Markale market on the 5th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing we noticed when studying the documents related to this incident was that there was a great discrepancy in the number of fatalities and the injured compared to the explosive power of one 120-millimetre shell. That was one thing. Also, it was highly unusual that in this area, which is rather large, the shell had fallen, unfortunately, or in whichever way, in the place where the concentration of people was the highest. We wondered how that was possible. Professionally and technically speaking, when we turned to the incident of the 28th August of the following year, it was practically impossible for the same thing to occur again. That was the first thing that struck us. And another thing that was astonishing was such a large number of people killed and injured, whereas the investigation was carried out very unprofessionally, very inaccurately, with many, many flaws. It was simply amazing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you tell us why you believe this investigation was carried out so inaccurately with many mistakes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it is strange that nobody noticed - and I must say the traces on the asphalt were not immediately visible - in the place where the stabiliser was embedded there was a large amount of rubble, which is practically impossible. The second unprofessional thing is that CSB investigators when they arrived were unable to find the place where the tail-fin was embedded and when we looked we realised there was a reason for that because that place is atypical and it does not have the normal features of a place where a stabiliser is embedded in its full length. Another unprofessional thing is that all the investigators were trying to determine the angle of descent using a method which does not exist as a method in our profession, and even when it is used, it was used in a way which is completely impermissible. That crater was dug over and over again, the stabiliser was put in it many times over - we don't know exactly what they did - Captain Verdy and the others did it, but nobody made the effort to determine the minimal possible angle, and the minimal angle is the angle which makes it possible for the shell to come to the place where it was activated without striking first any of the obstacles around. I can go on enumerating, but these would be the most important points that I remember at this moment. Probably in the course of further discussion I will remember more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let us look at figure 66 now in your report. It's on the English page 63; and in B/C/S, it's 92. For reference, this still was taken from P01899 at the time sequence 11 minutes, 09 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We ... and ... [Interpretation] Yes, up to 11 minutes, 10 seconds, so we can see these 2 seconds on the screen. I will ask my colleague Mr. Ivetic to play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you stop the video, it's always a little blurry. That's why we are using figure 66 from your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we have that picture back. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do we see on this video? Have you already explained?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was saying. Nobody noticed that in the spot where the explosion happened and the stabiliser embedded itself into the surface there was a mess of rubble which is completely unnatural there. It suggests it was placed there on purpose, that an explosion happened -- if an explosion had happened there and no one had brought anything, then the blast wave would have dispersed all of this and cleaned up the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at figure 69 on page 64 in English and 95 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do we see here?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A typical trace of a tail-fin of a 120-millimetre shell that landed there at a playground there in Dobrinja the previous day, and this is a typical example of what a crater should look like, and the crater at Markale should have looked the same way. You can see the whole tail-fin. And around it is the material that was pushed out when the tail-fin embedded itself into the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the surface like in this place compared to the one at Markale?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same kind. Below there is gravel and it's covered with asphalt on top.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it's page 82. We need figure 88. The English, page 82, and B/C/S, 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As the caption says, it's a stall as shown in the report of Berko Zecevic and the police report. Does this stall, in terms of appearance look the same as the stalls on the Markale market?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And that's one of the crucial things I omitted to mention before. This stall is completely different in shape and dimension compared to the stalls that we see on video recordings and are covered in this report. In my opinion, investigators should have studied it with great precision and accuracy because it's very important in order to determine whether it was possible for the shell to descend in that place without being activated first by any of the other stalls. That's the stall you see first on the pictures, not this one, which is completely different in shape and size.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at picture 3 from your report. In English, it's page 31, and in B/C/S, 35. Just as a reference this photograph is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to give a reference. Maybe my colleague [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber wanted to intervene already before you do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We might be thinking along the same lines. I noticed that there are a lot of different photographs from potentially different dates throughout the report, and already I think we could be assisted if there's some question posed to the witness or some indication as to what date or what the source of the image is when going through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Weber asks your specific attention for the time-frames.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This picture we can find in video marked as P01899 at time-frame 4 minutes, 50 seconds, and video is taken during the evacuation of wounded from this market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Weber is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It would suffice just to say on such and such a date [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 5th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, it's good to know exactly what still is presented here. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, what do we see on the photograph taken from this video?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to the people participating in the evacuation, we see the stall, and we see a row of stalls that were photographed from the side and the photograph 88 was also taken from the side. And you can see clearly that the stall is of a different shape and these metal supports are crossing on the stall, and in AutoCAD it was possible to measure angles at which these supports cross and determine the size of the stall. These measures are indicated on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These numbers on the photograph, from what time are they?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague and I added these numbers, and they represent angles at which these lateral supports are to the surface of the stall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at P868. It is a police file about the incident. It is already in evidence. First we need page 27 in the B/C/S. [In English] It's page 27 in English as well. We need the right page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this report, we have included the work of Mr. Sabljica. Can you see on this sketch the shape of the stall drawn by the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see it in the lower left-hand side corner. It is the same dimension as presented in Mr. Berkovic's report. During examination in the Karadzic case, we asked him how come the sketches were the same and Mr. Sabljica stated at the time - I think I even have a transcript reference - that they simply took the sketch of the stall from Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 37 of the report, please. It contains Mr. Zecevic's report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 8, line 10, it should have been Mr. Zecevic's report. The interpreter misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This comes from the same document as Mr. Zecevic's report. Can we see the same stall and does it have the same shape as in the police report.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the starting point concerning the type and shape of the stall was the same in the police report and the report by Mr. Zecevic. Are these dimensions correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not. The shape is not accurate. In our analysis, we had to accept that the width of the stall as well as its height was correct. However, as we can see in figure 3, it is incorrect, because the stall has a different shape, making its dimensions different when it comes to the actual roof and surface, as well as the distance between the edge of the roofing and the edge of the stall and so on and so forth. It impacts a number of other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that the roof is slanted on this sketch. In real life, were you able to ascertain that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In real terms, the roof is straight, as we can see in many stills from the footage. The best still is still number 11, taken from above. In figure 3 we saw a moment ago, we can see that the roof is straight. We can also see it very well there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us briefly look at figure 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's -- yeah, we moved from another document. It's 1D05496.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 41 -- page 41 in B/C/S and 33 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this the roofing of the stalls the way it was on the day of incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did look like this on the day of the incident, although this still is from an earlier period. In any case, it looked like this. This was taken before the incident, but I think there's also information in the report as to when the photograph was taken. Yes, it was published in the Glas Javnosti newspaper on the 13th of February, 2004. We don't know when the photograph was taken though. What is important to mention is that we can clearly see in picture 3 where we took the dimensions from that the roofing of the stalls is straight, level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask for clarification. Did you say, ma'am, this picture was taken on 13th of February, 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said that it was published in the newspaper on the 13th of February, 2004 and that we do not know when it was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, it's not known when it was taken. Okay. Thank you so much. Sorry, if we don't know when it was taken, how do we come to the conclusion that it was taken before the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was definitely taken before the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. But to say definitely doesn't answer my question. How do you come to that conclusion? You don't know when it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe we should see picture 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, no. I need an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was certainly taken even before the war because it is a well-frequented market-place. It certainly wasn't taken at the time of incident. I told you the source that we relied on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The source is published in 2004. Thank you very much. Certainly, definitely doesn't answer my question. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would still have a follow-up question. The only reason I heard you say is that it's a frequented market. Was it not frequented before the incident or was it not frequented after the incident? It's difficult to understand how a mere reference to being a frequented market allows you to say it was before or after the incident. Do you have a further explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. All of the footage taken during evacuation and at the time of incident indicates that most of the stalls were empty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the issue was that you say definitely it was before the incident, which then excludes the moment of the incident itself and the explanation you gave is that it was a frequented market. That allowed you to establish that time. We do not understand how -- I'm speaking for myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For all three of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For all three of us. We do not understand why a mere reference to the market being frequented allows you to say, It must have been before February 1994 or after February 1994. If you have an explanation, please give it; if you don't have one, then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we look at the photograph, we can see that, apart from being full of people, it is also full of goods, flowers and other things, that we could not find on the footage taken at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're moving away from what my question was. You're moving away from one of your previous answers. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have picture number 14 on our screens. It's page 44 in B/C/S and 34 in English. Just for the record, this picture comes from 65 ter number, Prosecution number -- actually it's exhibit already. P864. We have time stamp and date stamp on this video, 6th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this the layout of stalls that you found reflected the situation at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. It does not match the information recorded in the reports.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last sentence of your answer because the interpreters couldn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last sentence was this: This is the layout of stalls as at the time of incident, or the appearance of the stalls at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The first sentence of your answer was just the contrary of it. There you said, in answering Mr. Lukic's question: "No, it is not, it does not match the information recorded in the reports." Which of the two is true?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour. You should ask which report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I'm asking the witness. Compare the two answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the first part of my answer, I said that the shape of the stalls, as we can see it, does not reflect the shape of the stalls reported by the CSB and Mr. Berko Zecevic in his report. However, this is the appearance and position of the stalls at the time of incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This whole issue was triggered by a difference in phrasing the question and apparently how the question was understood. Mr. Lukic, you didn't ask does what we find here match with what we find in the reports. You asked is this the layout of the stalls at the time of the incident. The witness said no. Because she was thinking in terms of whether it matches with the reports, which, of course, is irrelevant but a different question. Could we try to carefully listen to the language which is used both in the question and when giving an answer, to be very precise in phrasing your words. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, did someone try to determine the minimal angle of descent in an attempt to discover what happened on the 5th of February, 1994 at Markale?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Save for Captain Verdy and Major Russell, nobody else tried to determine the minimal angle. The last day when the commission was set up, a minimal angle was determined. It was an UN commission. The angle was determined in relation to the UPI building but it is not an accurate minimal angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about members of the CSB or Mr. Berko Zecevic? Did they take interest in the damage to the stalls?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not look into that, which is surprising as well. Because we could see that the stalls were damaged. However, that damage does not fit with the traces that could have been caused by a shell or the shell that was investigated at the place they recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anyone tackle the stalls' damage?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did, quite extensively, and we raised that issue for the first time in the Karadzic case when we were examining my colleague, Mr. Berko Zecevic. On that occasion, Mr. Zecevic marked another place of explosion, which is in a street connecting Marsala Tita Street and Dzenetica Cikma Street. We provided that in our analysis. Perhaps this is a good time to say that there is a document in existence showing that on that day, the 5th of February, the Military Observers of the UN drafted a report indicating that there had been two explosions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just one question. The witness is now referring to testimony given by Mr. Zecevic in another case. Is that in evidence before us so that we can consider that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to locate it. It in this report, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But my question is whether what Mr. Zecevic said that he took another point of impact, if I understand well, than in the initial reports. Is that in evidence before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, could you first answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not in evidence yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not in evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have figure 94 from this report. It's page 129 in B/C/S, and it's 84 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can we see before us, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before us is the figure we mentioned showing the second place of explosion marked by my colleague, Mr. Berko Zecevic. However on that occasion he did not say that he investigated that spot. He just stated that it was the second place of explosion, the consequences of which may be seen on the red stall on the left side. Given the fact that this is a footage frame, we can see that on the other side there are also shrapnel marks on the rest of the stalls. It is footnote 305.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can we have 1D5685.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber has great difficulties in hearing the evidence of a witness commenting on matters which we do not know about, so, therefore, the logical sequence is that in one way or another, but perhaps you're going to do that, now I do not know whether you do this under what rule you are doing this for us to admit this into evidence or that you just want to read a few lines. We do not know. But apparently you take us back to what the basis of the evidence of the witness here is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is transcript from Karadzic trial, testimony of Berko Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. This is, therefore, not in evidence and if you want to tender that, we'll hear under what rule you will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will just read one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have some trouble with the possible transcript coming up in terms of the reference in the report, in terms of page numbers and what's the scope of it. So if counsel could assist. I don't know what portions he is going to direct to, but also if he could clarify the full range of Mr. Zecevic's discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 11 in this document from line 17. It should respond to transcript page 12318. So then it's the next page. Sorry. Page 12. I will be able to locate it more precisely. It's two pages. I've move on for now. I'll turn back to this issue. But I -- we just want to hear from the Prosecution whether they accept or do not accept what Mr. Zecevic marked during Karadzic trial and what we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I really don't know what Mr. Lukic is doing right now to accept or not accept something. So I mean, I'm kind of waiting to see where this goes. Still, I would appreciate over the break if I could know what the full range of the intended reference here is in footnote 306 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We had the same issue a couple of days ago. Do they accept what their witness said in previous trial or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is Mr. Zecevic their witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So what you're asking is whether they accept what a Prosecution witness in another case said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They were on the list but they never brought him, so he didn't testify in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore he is not a witness in this case. At least he didn't appear as a witness. Now, there are various levels of admitting. Is it that Mr. Weber accepts that he said what he's recorded as having said but then, of course, he needs to know exactly what portion you want to address. The second issue is whether Mr. Weber accepts for the truth of its content what Mr. Zecevic said. And then, again, Mr. Weber, I take it, needs to know exactly what lines, what words you are referring to. So, therefore, I think the question as it stands now, it's not a great surprise that Mr. Weber has not yet committed himself to any of it. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour has correctly identified the reasons and also just as probably the Chamber is aware, this could get quite complicated because is he another expert and there might be many section of transcript that might relate to a given issue. So if counsel could identify even the topic, what it relates to, things like that would be great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this -- I can, actually it would help if my colleague --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could do that during the break just so it's out of the presence of the witness that would be appreciated too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What's the secret. She read it. She has it in her report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, where are we looking? What footnote?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 23, line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And until page 24, line 22 [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that in the footnote?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... footnote 305 and 306.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Footnote 305, 306, where a reference is given. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER

utterances.text: In the translation. Okay. Then you take the original next to it and see whether we find different figures there.

utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you please -- could -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: Could you please give the page again because I think the stenographer missed it.

utterances.text: Okay. If counsel would sort out these matters, know exactly what the one is referring to and how the other should understand that, then we'll hear after the break. It's -- it looks like this. I would have expected one single calculation which fits on one line, explaining what it is. We'll have a look at, but this certainly is not just what I asked for. Madam Registrar, could you please copy it and have it distributed among the parties and for the Chamber over the break, or perhaps even during the break. We take a break. Witness, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we resume at 25 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe we should discuss before the witness is with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes, what should we discuss?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding this photo signed by Berko Zecevic. First we want to ask the Prosecution whether they stipulate what Mr. Zecevic marked on that photograph as one of the places of explosion or not.

utterances.text: That's two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do they stipulate that's what he marked as and the second is then does the Prosecution accept that to be in accordance with the truth. That's I think the two questions -- unless you would -- I mean, the first one is -- Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe counsel is oversimplifying the issue that we have right in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you do not stipulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, but if I could address the matter, please. Thank you, Your Honours. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps before the Tribunal but not for this Chamber of the Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and in this case. Yes, let me just summarise that you said a witness who did not testify before the Tribunal, you meant to say a witness who did not testify in this case before the Tribunal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, in reviewing the specific matter that comes up here, I reviewed transcript pages 12316, line 12, through 12320, line 22. What we see, what I found in that transcript portion is a discussion --

utterances.text: Mr. Weber, which transcript.

utterances.text: Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Of the Karadzic transcript of Mr. Zecevic and what he found in that is a discussion of a topic which eventually led to the display of an image that was not a part of Mr. Zecevic's report but from some other source and then Mr. Zecevic was put questions and asked to comment upon that photograph. In looking at that further, I went back to our present expert report paragraph 74 and I noticed a number of things that, I believe, makes it complicated for the Prosecution to simply agree or not agree on something. Just to give a quick example: In paragraph 74, Ms. Subotic states: "He" - referring to Mr. Zecevic - "also presented the thesis that the damage could have been caused by fragments which flew like a boomerang." Well, in going to the related transcript portion on this photograph, it is not Mr. Zecevic who presented that theory, it is Mr. Karadzic who asked the witness of that and then also gives an explanation as to why that is, that's rather lengthy in the Karadzic proceedings. So, simply asking the Prosecution do we agree whether he marked a photo or not without knowing the context or meaning of it I think is a quite a difficult thing to do and we're not going do that. That is our explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have at length explained now there is no stipulation. Mr. Lukic, that's where we stand. Any other matter before the witness is escorted into the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then did they inform the Karadzic Chamber that Mr. Zecevic did not mark correctly this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.text: I'm sorry, but this has been at the outset an inappropriate effort to circumvent all of the rules and procedures that govern the admission of evidence in this Chamber and now it's become almost an extortion effort by falsely claiming that it implicates some of the issues in the Karadzic case, and I think it should stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that a threat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's try to calm down again. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we can have Ms. Subotic with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I'd like to inquire whether the issue that came up yesterday of 1D01337, and more, in particular, page 9 of that document, whether that was already in evidence as D185 and I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the same source, it's similar but it's not the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We looked at it, and Mr. Lukic is correct. There's an attachment that's different. We have no objection because there is the slight difference if the second document was also tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number for 1D01337 was that assigned already? I don't remember. It was not. Could you please assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D01337 receives exhibit number D1263, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would just give me one second. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would start with Prosecution exhibit P864. It's a video. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can we have figure 94 from the report, 1D5496, please. It's English version 84 and B/C/S version 129.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, looking at your report, making your report, did you read the documentation and transcripts from the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What, in your view, did Mr. Berko Zecevic mark on this photo?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Berko Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. Relevance, facts not in evidence. And I don't know if this is even the most efficient way of proceeding since this witness is an expert herself she should be able to tell us what she sees in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She was not there in 1994. She has to use materials provided by Sarajevo police and Sarajevo expert, Berko Zecevic, who was admitted here, his report is admitted here in this case as part of the document P868, so it's not that Berko Zecevic does not have saying in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, you were not there on the 5th of February. Were you there when Mr. Zecevic testified in the Karadzic case. Were you present in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the witness may have knowledge, apart from whether that would compete with other sources of evidence, but the witness could tell us what she, at the time, heard and saw. Were you in the courtroom? Were you in the public gallery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Lukic, you may ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you proceed with the question. Your question was: What in your view, did Mr. Berko Zecevic mark on this photo? Do you want to say: What did you see him mark or do you want her to give a view or to say whether she saw him mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we know that Ms. Subotic saw him marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you can see something, you can -- yes, you should have done that, I think, in first instance to establish the source of knowledge. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps the Prosecution then, of course, has an opportunity to look in the transcript and see whether they agree with that or not. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you've heard the question of the Judges. Could you answer --

utterances.text: We've not put any question to the witness [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: I gave the framework which you can -- the limits within which you can ask a question to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did you see at that time while you were in the courtroom? What did Mr. Berko Zecevic mark? Let's begin with number 1.

utterances.text: With number 1, he marked the site of the second explosion, the one we did not investigate.

utterances.text: Also in a circle, if I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. That's right.

utterances.text: I'm just losing time. I'm going my way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand Your Honours' instructions. It's just we are sensitive of time and you know our position; this is not relevant at this stage. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should we act as the Prosecution feels?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the objection at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there was no objection, first of all, there was an invitation to give what the Prosecution thinks is the complete context. You're not doing that. You're doing it your way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Later we'll find out, I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.text: It's a different site of the explosion. It's not the one he investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... pages correspond? I have some doubt.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] So do I.

utterances.text: Can we see page 42, then, in English version.

utterances.text: Now we have the same document twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now it definitely matches. It's previous page in English version.

utterances.text: We have two pages in an English version of this document, so ...

utterances.text: The English page is in the B/C/S version as well. I may take it that it's got something to do with the table mainly having numbers rather than text, but I leave it your hands, Mr. Lukic, how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you able to use this English table?

utterances.text: I know that I extracted it and put it in the report. Lima reported two explosions. I'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see at least page 42 in English version. Or the previous one. Because it says here 43 of 46. I don't know how it's uploaded. But we need the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll move on. We'll perhaps come back to it later. Let's not waste time. We will now watch a film made by the police in Sarajevo. That's 1D5916.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll continue with P864. I'm sorry for this delay. And we just need a -- this still which is on 25 minutes, 28 seconds.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see it on the screen, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can we see on this picture; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The impact of shrapnel on the stall in the wall behind it. So from the side and from the front and the wall behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From this side, is the damage the greatest?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this side, which is longer and parallel to the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness you're saying "from this side," "from that side," we don't know which side you are referring to. utterances.text: Can we have help of the usher so Ms. Subotic can mark what she is telling us.

utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I don't know if would be okay to take a screen capture and then show the witness the screen capture, mark on it.

utterances.text: Yes, but then someone has to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you are referring to a certain side of a stall, then we'll try to find it with the cursor and then I'll make an attempt to describe it properly. Okay. So let's start again. If you want to [Microphone not activated]

utterances.text: Can't we take a --

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: -- caption of this video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, someone has to do that. So if you can do it, please do it. Of course, you should have done it most likely before being in court confronted with the problem.

utterances.text: Let's, for the time being, because the Registry is unable to make a screen shot at this moment from this video. You haven't prepared it. So let's do it with what we have. That is, a still from the video, and we have an usher who is able to move the cursor. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's Mr. Ivetic who has to handle the cursor. But let's try to get where we ought to be. That is, to hear the relevant evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, can you describe where you see more damage, on what side?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see more damage on the long side of the white stall to the front of the picture. Yes, this is the damage. That damage also appears along the longer side of the stall towards the upper edge.

utterances.text: The source of the explosion must be where it was launched from.

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: The impact, yes. Could you tell us where in relation to this picture the impact of the projectile was.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] The impact of the projectile investigated as part of the incident is to the side and left, around the corner we can see, placed vertically next to number 13.

utterances.text: Let's first take it step by step. You said to the side. Could the cursor be moved to the place where you ... it's there. Were you referring to that? Or I see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but around the edge. Around the corner. There.

utterances.text: Yes.
