utterances.text: I believe you. Somebody tampered the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I did apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not only do you believe but you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I'll ask Ms. Subotic about what she saw before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. What she -- I have screwed it in now again. I missed my real profession, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was just quite a claim that was made by Mr. Lukic. I mean, if he has got a good-faith base to assert that it has been tampered with. Otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, it's always better to present the evidence for your claims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then hear -- Mr. Weber is not yet convinced, I do understand. Keep it here for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you mentioned the number which referred to the Markale II tail-fin and I think you said you needed the other one but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I thought they were both under the same number. I don't have the other number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, are they both under the same number which, as a matter of fact, would be a perfect scenario for confusion, but the tail-fin I have in my hands at this moment bears on a sticker the number A000-6279. And is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that is Exhibit D409.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D409. Madam Registrar, could you please check whether D409, indeed, is an artefact, the tail-fin of a ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar has confirmed that D409, which is the tail-fin of Markale I, was last -- the last -- the second given to us and which we have now in our hands and for which I read the number. We keep it for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is right, it is D409, Your Honour. I apologise for not having the right number with me. Can we give that tail-fin, D409, to Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the witness needs it, then... The artefact, D409, is now given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, without our permission, you're not allowed to change it in any way. I did it before, but without our permission, you're not allowed to do it. So you can look at it, you can have it in your hands, and wait for the questions that Mr. Lukic will put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought we would have this line of questioning only for the second artefact, but I have to ask you the same questions about this one too. So, we saw the charge was able to very easily unscrew it manually, the base charge. Did you ever hold that particular tail-fin in your hands?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is now D409.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. It's confusing if we say the first and the second. Please use the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We call it in this courtroom, D409. You have had it in your hands before?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the occasion when you held it, did you check if you were able to turn the base charge?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, were you able to unscrew the base charge?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And it was not to be expected that I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was that you held it in your hands and you checked that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember the date. We could maybe look through the photos we made at the time and see the date on the photo. But it was at the beginning of the Karadzic trial when I travelled together with Mr. Sladojevic, Prosecutor Gaynor, and somebody from the Registry, I can't remember the name, and then I made a photo documentation of this evidence which is now before the Court. There were also some remnants of shrapnel, et cetera, so these photographs you see here in the report were made at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you are talking about figure 80; correct? In your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 80, 82, and 83.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us who were present when you tried to take off the lower part or the primary -- Mr. Lukic, had you a better word for it. You've forgotten it, but ... the base --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Base charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who were present when you tried that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marko Sladojevic, from the Defence team of Mr. Karadzic; Prosecutor Gaynor; and somebody from the Registry. I don't know who. Somebody who brought it into that room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us how you tried to move the base charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a way similar to what you did without any particular tools. Mr. Sladojevic tried to do the same thing on that occasion, finding it interesting. However, the lack of my technical knowledge in that area would not allow it. To tell you the truth, I checked it out of professional curiosity rather than because I expected it to be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said you didn't use any particular tools. Did you use any tool at all, such-like a ballpoint as Judge Fluegge did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I had with me a pencil to take notes. I did not try to apply any force to open it. I don't think Mr. Sladojevic tried to apply a pen either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then for the completeness of the record, I have hereby to put on the record that I tried to twist it with my fingers and after I was unsuccessful to do that, Judge Fluegge, after perhaps a few seconds seeing what I was doing, used his Bic ballpoint, I think it is. It's here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: A traditional which is used in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Used it. And it was only then that the base charge started to be twisted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that technically it was impossible to do. Can you explain to us what kind of force one needs to use to be able to turn the base charge after an explosion, especially now that we have seen it in both cases for Markale I and II?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you be -- I missed exactly where the witness said that technically she was -- it was unable to do it. Could you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 56, line 3. It says: "However the lack of my technology in that area would not allow it." So I don't know if it's the answer, the lack of my technology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's something different from what you put to the witness, so would you be very precise in the phrasing of your question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We believe the interpretation was technical knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, what did you say? Why were you not -- what did you say? Why was it that did you not try to use a pencil but you only tried it by hand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we have to first clarify the transcript. The interpreters made a note we believe the interpretation was and then again the same difference between the words spoken and the transcript occurs. Can we ask the interpreters to again repeat what they said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We believe the original interpretation was technical knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is exactly what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have two steps, Mr. Lukic, you know that. The first is the audio and then the second is then the interpretation of what was heard by our interpreters. If you ask any further questions to the witness, if you are telling us now what you said before, please be aware that we have the technical means to verify what you said before, and that's what often when we do there's any dispute about what was said or not. Mr. Lukic will now put his next question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do you remember what was it that you said?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that based on my technical knowledge, which is primarily based on my knowledge in -- as to how the shell is produced and used, I did not feel any need to do so because I wanted simply to be able to check and verify the entire artefact or piece of evidence, not just partially. That is why I did not use any tools. On the other hand, Marko Sladojevic found it very interesting and did try to insert a pen, turning it and ultimately there were a few of us there, and it can always be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you used the pen, did it turn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what kind of force must be applied to unscrew the base charge after the shell had exploded?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I need to provide a short introduction in order to answer. There's no difference in the possibility to unscrew the base charge before or after the explosion technically speaking, because during the explosion there is no such force that would influence the possibility of unscrewing the base charge. That is one thing. Another thing that is very important to understand is this. When the shell is manufactured, the base charge is screwed in by using tools and a lot of force. The actual screw is lubricated by a type of cement, particular cement, which provides for further contact. Hence, there is no possibility whatsoever that something of this sort would happen without an intervention that had nothing to do with the explosion and forces involved. There is no technical ability to do so given the type of manufacture. Those who design shells must make sure that it will not fall apart in mid air. The forces that occur at explosion are axial and the tail is simply ripped off. There is no torsion that would result in a possible unscrewing. Ultimately, Mr. Turkusic testified to the very same in this case. He explained it much the same way I did and he has significantly more field experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness refers to something that, as far as I remember, is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Mr. Turkusic testified in our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll look. Forgive me for not having every piece of evidence constantly on the top of my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: After the introduction, can you answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I'll tell you. Your question was: So what kind of force must be applied to unscrew the base charge after the shell has exploded? The answer was: I apologise I need to provide a short introduction in order to answer. Now the short introduction which was fairly long has been given. Now I'm waiting now for the answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, you heard it. Would you mind answering.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought my long introduction resulted in an answer at the end. It is this: The force that needs to be applied is torque which does not occur at the time of explosion or immediately afterwards. One would have to use torsion to unscrew it, much as with any other kind of nut and bolt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that you are embedding in your answer something which was not part of the question. That as -- that is, whether there would be any force produced during and after firing, which would be sufficient to unscrew. The question, however, simply was what force is needed to unscrew. In whatever way, by your hands, by a tool, by -- and you are limiting your answer to an unscrewing during flight without manipulation but just on the basis of the forces exercised in itself. Could you please now answer the question: What force is needed to unscrew it? If you know. If you say, I can't tell you, that's fine as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the flight and explosion and the period after the explosion, there is no force which could unscrew this without further manipulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay. What force is needed? And include force by manipulation. What force is needed to unscrew it? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In terms of type, it would be torque, or turning. In terms of intensity, it would have to be at least at the level used by the tools to tighten the base charge and attach it to the body of the shell. I can check that in our documentation and, off the cuff, I don't know what amount of force is needed, but it is a lot, in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did your calculations for Markale I with this stabilising fin that does not unscrew; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I rose and the answer came already, but that was a very leading question, and it's not exactly transparent what calculations we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's both leading and unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I haven't asked yet any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You told her that she did her calculations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, I read: "You did your calculations for Markale I which was with the stabiliser fin that does not unscrew; is that correct?" The question is "is that correct," and the leading part is where you told the witnesses what she had done. So that makes together a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in terms of your Markale I report, did you believe that the base charge cannot be unscrewed and that is how you approached the artefact?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While comparing and trying to prove that there were two stabilisers, we worked under the presumption that the base charge could not be unscrewed, that it was fixed to the body of the stabiliser, which is a technical fact that is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. My next question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask one follow-up question. You earlier told us that during flight no force is exercised at all about the base charge. Did the question whether or not the base charge could be relatively easily unscrewed or not, did that play any role in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only while comparing this piece of evidence in the courtroom and the stabiliser used in the field by the commission with Mr. Berko Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you mean by the identification of the tail-fin you had in your hands here and the -- or the -- and the photograph but not in terms of -- not in terms of distance or angles or whatever. That was not -- it was not an issue in those calculations, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was not an issue in determining the angle of descent and the distance of firing. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time when you were examining it, did you take photographs while you were examining D409?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that we used them in the paper. These are figures 80, 83, 82. They are the figures representing what I created at that moment on the premises of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you took the picture, the position of the base charge was as shown in figure 80, or was it not?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, that's the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The tail-fin is before you. Was it embedded in the ground - the one before you - along its entire length and, in your view, would that have been possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. Compound question and it is also, in part, leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is another matter that it requires exactly the basis of the knowledge whether the witness answers your question on basis of photographs or personal observation. Could you split it up, Mr. Lukic [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that's why I directed the attention of Ms. Subotic to the artefact so she tells us based on the artefact she is holding in her hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- on the basis of something that you have in your hands, you cannot, in itself - and it's not sufficient basis of knowledge - to tell anyone where that artefact has been a year ago, or two years ago. So, therefore, it is an element in establishing that but it's an insufficient basis of knowledge of where it was a year ago. It helps to establish if you have other knowledge to compare whether it's this one, which matches your other source of knowledge, that is, where it was a year ago. So, therefore, try to keep things very clear and split up your question and we'd like to hear the answers. Because we're interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, based on the artefact, D409, can you determine if it was embedded anywhere in asphalt or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is -- we have to wait for the answer first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Weber is on his feet. He may object. And if he wants to object he has an opportunity to do so. He is not expected to comment. The question was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just give a legal basis. I think it goes along with what Your Honours were just saying, foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Foundation is the issue. But let's first --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot put this question differently. We have to wait for the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the artefact I have in my hands, I would say that there is practically impossible that this object remained embedded in the ground as the type of ground that we can see in Markale I which is a type of asphalt. Because on the cylindrical part which is the first to be embedded, we see absolutely no traces, no longitudinal truces of such penetration. It is interesting, though, that it does bear some markings that resemble the markings of a file but there are no longitudinal marks whatsoever. One must understand that this is the first part that penetrates at great force and speed into some solid material comprised of gravel, and this would have left longitudinal markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you previously held the tail-fin in your hands, did you also notice that there were no longitudinal scratches on the base of the tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is clear on the photographs we provided; in photograph 80, as well as 83.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ultimately, what did you conclude based -- concerning the incident at Markale on the 5th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on detailed analysis amounting to over 100 pages, we concluded - and also having reconstructed the shape of the stall and the layout of stalls in the market-place, as well as having found that there was a stall which contained damage from below and the reports by Russell and Verdy whose reports are provided in copy in our report - it was our conclusion that the explosion was caused by a static 120-millimetre shell which did not detonate following a flight path but was, rather, activated in some other unorthodox manner. We also took into account the other explosion that whose marks or traces exist marked by Mr. Zecevic and we discussed it today in the courtroom. I believe it is figure 80. 85. And ... 94.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a reference, the picture showing an overturned stall is figure 71.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how come that, under such circumstances, the tail-fin was found under or below ground level, surface level?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technical explanation was provided. If we recall the site where the tail-fin was embedded, it contained practically no traces of the tail-fin being embedded. The hole had been dug up and the tail-fin was simply placed there as used by Mr. Zecevic. I stand by my assertion that there were two tail-fins. Some soil was then put in the hole and the shell was placed in it, detonating it later on in an unorthodox fashion. The fact is that the shell could not have fallen on the area. It is supported by the fact that are no longitudinal traces, as well as -- there's -- it's also a fact that the area where this tail-fin was apparently embedded was an unusual area or of unusual surface. That was our conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one additional question to that. I understood your last answer to be an explanation of the earlier sentence, that the explosion was caused by a static 120-millimetre shell. In your view, what do you think how the explosion was triggered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, it could have been done by electrical impulse; for example, by using a TNT bullet or in some other way. We do it at firing ranges frequently when we carry out testing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you find anywhere - in the reports or on the site or at the artefact - any signs of that possibility that it was triggered by an electrical impulse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean in the sense that traces of such a device were found on the site? Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On the site, mentioning -- mentioned in the report, or at the artefact itself. Anywhere.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except on the artefact where there are no traces of penetration on the cylindrical part. I didn't find anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also have a few follow-up questions. Do I have to understand if it was a static body that exploded, or a projectile, whatever, that it must have exploded above ground level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, therefore, must have been visible, if it was placed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very simple to make. You set it at an angle, and to be quite clear, traces on the spot and the measurements of the crater show that it was at an angle, you place a box on top. It's a market, for God's sake. It could be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And everyone who was there stayed there. Everyone sees a projectile body to be put somewhere amidst the stalls, and then everyone waits until it exploded? I mean, I'm trying to imagine what you have on your mind in this alternative scenario.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this alternative scenario, I only have one technical possibility after all the analysis that were performed. And that is it. It could not land, this thing did not embed itself. It is not possible for so many people to have been killed. We saw traces all around. This is the only explanation. It could not land without hitting anything else before. Our analysis were detailed. Then there were traces under the stalls. Under these tables of the stalls. This is the only technical possibility that remains. I'm not going into anybody's scenario.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's then the end of the day, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Because we have one half an hour longer than usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we started half an hour later. We'll take a break, and, we'd like to see you back at quarter past 2.00, Ms. Subotic, and then we'll have another half an hour to go for this day. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Resume at quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we are going to move to incident of 28 August 1995; Markale II. That part of the report begins on page 96 in English and 141 in B/C/S. Would you please tell us, while we're waiting for it to appear on the screen, what are the features of the explosion of 28 August 1995 on the Markale market?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 28 August 1995 incident outside the market in Mula Mustafa Baseskija Street is characterised by similar features as on the Markale I incident. One shell exploded, and again, it landed exactly on the spot where there were the most people. Compared to the investigation on Markale I market, this investigation is even less accurate and inconsistent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, would you allow me to ask one question. Witness - and it's not the first time you said it - "the shell exactly landed where there were the most people." Now, I do understand that a market where there are a lot of people, but did you -- is that what you wanted to express? Or did you think that just around where the explosion took place that there were more people than, well, let's say, 100 metres away, or -- I'm not fully understanding what you mean by "they exploded on the spot where there were the most people"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the part of the market where there were the most people. On Markale I market, and the part of the market with the highest concentration of people because that's where the street vendors were located, close to the spot where the shell landed and exploded outside the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, my question is: How do you know how the people were divided or distributed over those market areas, well, let's say, a second before the explosion? How did you know there were more close to the explosion and less at a distance of 20 or 50 metres or -- what's the basis of your knowledge for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the Markale market, the basis is the type and concentration of goods. The rest of the market was empty. We can see that on the photos made after the evacuation. And the rest of the market was covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a follow-up. What then must be inferred from the fact that it exploded where there was a concentration of people? Obviously lots of people in the market. What is so uncharacteristic about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is uncharacteristic is that in both incidents, the explosions happened on the spots with the highest concentration of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But -- you're giving my question as my answer. As the answer. I'm asking you, yes, so what? What must we infer from that? Because you're mentioning this as a criticism in the way the investigation was made as conducted by those who investigated this. I'm just trying to found out what inference must be drawn from the fact that it fell where there was a concentration of people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First and foremost, I just made that as an observation, not as criticism of the on-site investigation. I'm going to express criticism of the on-site investigation later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the fact that you mentioned, are the factors which made you conclude that the market was not evenly crowded but that it was specifically a concentration of people where that shell exploded. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not receive English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, why do you believe this investigation was carried out in a wrong and inaccurate way? The Judges have now heard the question. You can answer.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, in this case, the explosion outside the market, the angle of descent was wrongly determined although using a different method than on the Markale market, but it's still wrong. Second, the determination of the direction that was made was not documented in any way. Third, the discrepancy between UNPROFOR and the observers is recorded in the material we have already used, in their statements. That is to say, the material that contains their reports. Also, it is not documented how come the shell landed on the market without any radar around Sarajevo recording the sound. The explanation given in the reports concerning the radar is technically senseless. It is not explained in any way how the shell came in without the radar noticing. It is also nowhere explained how in different stages of the investigation the direction of fire was determined variously as 220 degrees, then 170, then 160. It was also recorded that there were two tail-fins on the site and that is also recorded on video. There was no investigation within the market, although there were injured victims inside. We also have video footage which is technically inexplicable and that is that next to the curb and closer to the road there is shattered glass from the explosion. It is inexplicable how it found its way there. It should be concentrated along the wall. A little maybe, but not there. Those are all points that should have been clarified by the investigation, whoever performed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at photograph 97 from your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English page 98 and page 145 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the 65 ter number being?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on our screens, Your Honour. It's 1D5496.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not dwell on this too long --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We won't dwell on this. We have seen before in this trial this injured man whose body is hanging over the bar, the fence. In your analysis, did you find him in the documentation recorded as a fatality?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this injury that we see was inflicted by something which is certainly not a mortar or artillery projectile, we searched through the photo documentation, and this obviously dead man was not found among those injured or killed in the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does that fact show in terms of the investigation? Do you have any conclusion as to how this man with this type of injury found himself there?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man with this type of injury could not be there due to the explosion of the shell outside the market, and this injury could not have been inflicted by the explosion regardless of how close or how far he was from the explosion. This is rather close. But the main thing is that this type of injury cannot be sustained from an artillery or mortar projectile. All I can conclude is that he was brought here from somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that there's been some discussion now from the witness about the man. Could we have an identity of who he is?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All I can say and I identified that way that he was hanging over this fence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you ask the witness, perhaps, whether she knows who this person is, whether he was ever identified. Perhaps she could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I said a moment ago that we searched through the list of those injured and fatalities, and he is not among the list of fatalities so we were not able to identify him. Neither on the lists or the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you want to find a person on a list with names, then the starting point would be that you have a name, which you search for on that list. I'm -- we're trying to understand what you're telling us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll explain. In the photo documentation, there are photographs of all those who were killed, and that man is not any of the photographs of fatalities, and all of them who are in the document have been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And he's not in the document? If I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know what happened with this body? I mean, whether brought there or how -- do you have any knowledge about this person with which one would assume is not alive anymore with these jeans, what happened to him; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any basis for assuming that he was brought there rather than that he was killed on the spot, apart from you didn't find him or a similar person on the list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My opinion that he was brought there is based upon the fact that the blood-stain in front of his hands is symbolic. If it had happened there, there would have been a huge amount of blood pouring onto this fence over which he is hanging. On the other hand, he could not have thrown by the explosion to land in this position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, to land in this position, he would have had to have his arms raised at the moment of the explosion. And during the explosion, the person is simply propelled backwards in the position in which he is standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And he had not his arms raised during the explosion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying that people normally don't raise their arms during the explosion. That's not the kind of a reaction a blast wave causes. In the position in which they are already standing, they are propelled to one side, and if -- to land in this way, he would have had to have his arms fully in the air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all hypothetical. You do not know whether he had raised his hands at the moment of the impact. You don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How he lands as he has landed, you said he would have been thrown backwards, doesn't that depend on which side, whether the back or front of him, the explosion took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right. Whichever way he was facing, he would have been thrown backwards relative to the centre of the explosion. That is to say, away from the explosion. What tells me that he was brought here is that his arms are hanging over the fence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So if -- if -- if the explosion took place behind him and it throws him away from the explosion and he falls forward, he could fall and his arms could hang over the railing like he is without him necessarily having raised his arms? Thank you so much. If you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, but the explosion did not happen behind him. It was further down the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ah, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I don't know how you know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I need a -- two or three minutes for a matter. Therefore, I suggest that we adjourn for the day. Witness, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 again - so not at 10.00 - in the same courtroom. And I give you the same instructions as I did yesterday and the day before yesterday, that is that you should not -- we were not here on Sunday but last week that you should not communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to briefly deal with a scheduling issue. Last week, the parties have made submissions in court in relation to scheduling matters. The Defence made submissions in relation to its two Tomasica experts and the filing of their reports. The Chamber understands that one of these two proposed experts is Witness Radovanovic and thus expects that the Defence will file a motion to recall that witness. In addition, the Chamber instructs the Defence to give weekly updates on the progress of the two expert reports. The updates can be given orally or in writing, and the first update is due on the 2nd of October. On Friday, the Defence filed a motion asking the Chamber to set a deadline for the final Defence bar table motion to two months and 12 days after the testimony of the last Defence witness as that was the time-frame in which the Prosecution filed its last bar table motion. The Chamber recalls that its guidance on bar table submission was clarified on 29 March 2012 at transcript pages 234 to 236. The Chamber clarified that bar table motions should not be filed at the end of a party's case but at the end of individual components of a party's case. The reason for this was exactly to avoid a situation as the current one, where all remaining documents are collected to be tendered. In addition, ensuring equality of arms is not a matter of mathematics, especially considering the Prosecution's evidentiary burden. The Chamber notes that while the Prosecution filed a total of three bar table motions within two months and 12 days of the hearing of its last witness, the tendering in the later two of its motions was limited in volume with around some 120 documents in total, and almost exclusively concerned documents which had previously been tendered and denied. In fact, the second residual bar table motion of the Prosecution tendered documents denied 11 days earlier in a decision by the Chamber. Furthermore, the Prosecution filed about 65 per cent of its bar table documents prior to the hearing of its last witness, and 97 per cent within one week of the testimony of this last witness. Considering the above, pursuant to Rule 90(F), the Chamber sets a deadline for the Defence's final bar table motion to be filed by the 18th of January, 2016. The Defence is further instructed to organise the list of documents to tender from the bar table by the components of the case, as well as by Scheduled Incident, where applicable. Further, the Defence is strongly encouraged to share with the Prosecution at the earliest possibility which documents will be tendered so as to allow the Prosecution to be most efficient and expeditious when responding to the motion. In relation to Tomasica, considering that the testimony of the two proposed expert witnesses is still forthcoming, the Chamber decides that any bar table motion in relation to Tomasica be filed no later than one week after the hearing of the final Defence proposed expert in relation to Tomasica. That was the scheduling issue I wanted to deal with. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 30th of September, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
